'''Michel Lazdunski''' (born 11 April 1938, in [[Marseille]]) is a French [[biologist]] specializing in  [[biochemistry]], [[physiology]], [[pathophysiology]], [[Molecular Pharmacology|molecular pharmacology]] and [[neuroscience]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Université côte d'Azur|url=http://univ-cotedazur.fr/fr/contents/chercheurs/lazdunski-michel|date=}}</ref>
__TOC__

== Biography ==
Michel Lazdunski is a [[chemical engineer]] (1955), graduate of the École nationale supérieure de chimie de [[Clermont-Ferrand]], [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in Chemistry-Physics from [[Université Laval|Laval University]] in [[Quebec City]] (1962) in Canada in the laboratory of Ludovic Ouellet, then PhD in biochemistry ([[University of Marseille]], 1964). He began his career at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] in 1962 in Marseille where he became Professor of Biochemistry in 1965. He accepted the Chair of Biochemistry at the [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis|University of Nice]] in 1968. He founded the CNRS Biochemistry Centre there, which he managed until 1989, when he moved to the Sophia Antipolis science park to direct the CNRS Institute of Molecular and Cellular Pharmacology, which he had just created and which he managed until 2004. During his academic career in Nice/Sophia Antipolis, he was successively Professor of Biochemistry (Faculty of Sciences), Director of Research seconded to the CNRS and Professor of Pharmacology PU-PH (Faculty of Medicine).Michel Lazdunski was a member of the Scientific Council (1997–2001) and the Board of Directors (2001–2005) of the CNRS and the Council of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization|European Molecular Biology Organisation]] (1990–1995). He has chaired many committees including the UNECE Life Sciences Committee (Human Capital and Mobility Programme 1996–1997) and the National Coordinating Committee for Life Sciences (2001–2002).{{citation needed|date=March 2020}}

He was elected a full member of the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]] in 1991.<ref>{{cite web|title=Académie des sciences|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-L/michel-lazdunski.html|date=}}</ref> He was appointed senior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France|Institut universitaire de France]] in 1991 for a five-year term,<ref>{{cite web |title=Arrêté du 2 décembre 1991 portant nomination à l'Institut universitaire de France |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/affichTexte.do?cidTexte=JORFTEXT000000538896 |website=Legifrance |accessdate=8 March 2020}}</ref> renewed in 1996.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arrêté du 8 août 1996 portant nomination des membres seniors et juniors de l'Institut universitaire de France |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/affichTexte.do?cidTexte=JORFTEXT000000744248 |website=Legifrance |accessdate=8 March 2020}}</ref>

== Scientific contribution ==
The first part of Michel Lazdunski's scientific career (awarded the [[CNRS Silver Medal]]) was devoted to [[Enzyme|enzymology]]. He then focused on exploring the molecular machines, the [[ion channel]]s, that generate [[bioelectricity]] in the [[brain]], [[peripheral nervous system]], [[heart]], [[muscle]]s, vessels and hormone-secreting endocrine systems and are responsible for multiple pathologies.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|title=Michel Lazdunski-Research gate|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Michel_Lazdunski|date=}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Google scholar id|X-1_6w8AAAAJ}}</ref> He played a pioneering role in the analysis of ion channels permeable to [[sodium]], [[calcium]] and [[potassium]]. He played a pioneering role in the study of their pharmacology by introducing many [[toxin]]s, many venoms and important drugs for [[hypertension]] (calcium blockers) or [[diabetes]] (antidiabetic [[sulfonylurea]]s)<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name="Amoroso Schmid-Antomarchi Fosset Lazdunski pp. 852–854">{{cite journal | last1=Amoroso | first1=Salvatore | last2=Schmid-Antomarchi | first2=Heidy | last3=Fosset | first3=Michel | last4=Lazdunski | first4=Michel | title=Glucose, Sulfonylureas, and Neurotransmitter Release: Role of ATP-Sensitive K + Channels | journal=Science | publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) | volume=247 | issue=4944 | date=16 February 1990 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.2305257 | pages=852–854| pmid=2305257 | bibcode=1990Sci...247..852A }}</ref> The most recent work of his team has completed these pharmacological studies and amplified the discovery of new substances from venom with strong potential therapeutic possibilities. They have also led to the discovery of several new classes of ion channels essential for the sensory perception of mechanical stimuli, heat, cold and acidity. TREK/TRAAK channels, TASK channels and ASIC channels.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name="Waldmann Champigny Bassilana Heurteaux 1997 pp. 173–177">{{cite journal | last1=Waldmann | first1=Rainer | last2=Champigny | first2=Guy | last3=Bassilana | first3=Frédéric | last4=Heurteaux | first4=Catherine | last5=Lazdunski | first5=Michel | title=A proton-gated cation channel involved in acid-sensing | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=386 | issue=6621 | year=1997 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/386173a0 | pages=173–177| pmid=9062189 | bibcode=1997Natur.386..173W | s2cid=4361943 }}</ref> These families of channels play an essential role in pain perception but also in [[Neurotransmission|synaptic transmission]] and [[neuroprotection]] at the cerebral level, particularly for [[polyunsaturated fatty acid]]s of the ɯɜ type. TREK channels play a central role in depression.<ref name="Heurteaux Lucas Guy El Yacoubi pp. 1134–1141">{{cite journal | last1=Heurteaux | first1=Catherine | last2=Lucas | first2=Guillaume | last3=Guy | first3=Nicolas | last4=El Yacoubi | first4=Malika | last5=Thümmler | first5=Susanne | last6=Peng | first6=Xiao-Dong | last7=Noble | first7=Florence | last8=Blondeau | first8=Nicolas | last9=Widmann | first9=Catherine | last10=Borsotto | first10=Marc|author11-link=Gabriella Gobbi | last11=Gobbi | first11=Gabriella | last12=Vaugeois | first12=Jean-Marie | last13=Debonnel | first13=Guy | last14=Lazdunski | first14=Michel | title=Deletion of the background potassium channel TREK-1 results in a depression-resistant phenotype | journal=Nature Neuroscience | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=9 | issue=9 | date=13 August 2006 | issn=1097-6256 | doi=10.1038/nn1749 | pages=1134–1141| pmid=16906152 | s2cid=22729624 }}</ref> The TASK and TREK channels are a major therapeutic target for gaseous anesthetics.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name="Patel Honoré Lesage Fink 1999 pp. 422–426">{{cite journal | last1=Patel | first1=Amanda J. | last2=Honoré | first2=Eric | last3=Lesage | first3=Florian | last4=Fink | first4=Michel | last5=Romey | first5=Georges | last6=Lazdunski | first6=Michel | title=Inhalational anesthetics activate two-pore-domain background K+ channels | journal=Nature Neuroscience | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=2 | issue=5 | year=1999 | issn=1097-6256 | doi=10.1038/8084 | pages=422–426| pmid=10321245 | s2cid=23092576 }}</ref>

Previously, Michel Lazdunski and his team had made pioneering discoveries on the CFTR<ref name=":1" /><ref name="Dalemans Barbry Champigny Jallat 1991 pp. 526–528">{{cite journal | last1=Dalemans | first1=Wilfried | last2=Barbry | first2=Pascal | last3=Champigny | first3=Guy | last4=Jallat | first4=Sophie | last5=Jallat | first5=Sophie | last6=Dott | first6=Karin | last7=Dreyer | first7=Dominique | last8=Crystal | first8=Ronald G. | last9=Pavirani | first9=Andréa | last10=Lecocq | first10=Jean-Pierre | last11=Lazdunski | first11=Michel | title=Altered chloride ion channel kinetics associated with the ΔF508 cystic fibrosis mutation | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=354 | issue=6354 | year=1991 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/354526a0 | pages=526–528| pmid=1722027 | bibcode=1991Natur.354..526D | s2cid=4233457 | doi-access=free }}</ref> channel associated with [[cystic fibrosis]], which indicated the direction to follow for current therapeutic developments on some forms of this [[Genetic disorder|genetic disease]].
